Duration::floor¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::floor(std::string_view unit) const;

Retreat To A Unit Boundary¶

floor() replaces each lane with the greatest exact multiple of unit that is not greater than the original elapsed value. It is the operation to use when a duration must be assigned to a completed fixed-width interval.

The accepted, case-sensitive spellings are "ns", "us", "ms", "s", "min", "h", "D", and "W". Days and weeks mean fixed elapsed widths, not calendar periods. The result is newly allocated, has the same shape as the receiver, and preserves every NaT lane.

For negatives, floor moves toward negative infinity. Thus -0.5 s floors to -1 s, not zero. This agrees with the normalized component model where a negative sub-day span occupies the preceding whole day plus nonnegative sub-day fields.

Examples¶

Example 1. Floor a mixed vector to complete seconds.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos({
    -1'600'000'000LL, -1'500'000'000LL, -500'000'000LL,
     500'000'000LL,  1'500'000'000LL, 2'500'000'000LL,
     1'400'000'000LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT,
});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.floor("s").total().nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[-2.0000e+09, -2.0000e+09, -1.0000e+09, 0.0000e+00, 1.0000e+09, 2.0000e+09, 1.0000e+09, nan]

Example 2. The same value can be bucketed at any canonical width.

auto value = pluss::duration::nanos(93'784'005'006'007LL);
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(value.floor("h"));

Output¶

Duration(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1)
1 days 02:00:00.000000000

Using "ns" would leave that value unchanged; "us" and "ms" discard only finer fractions; "D" produces exactly one day.

Example 3. Scalar rank and N-D shape are both preserved.

auto matrix = pluss::duration::nanos({1, -1, 1'500'000'000, -1'500'000'000},
                                     {2, 2});
auto result = matrix.floor("s");
// result.sizes() == [2,2]

An unsupported spelling throws Duration: unsupported unit; no lane is returned with an inferred unit.

See Also¶

  • ceil(): move to the boundary at or above each value.

  • round(): select the nearest boundary.
